Fixed assets and depreciation

Ties the asset register to the books, works out this month's book depreciation from your policy, finds disposals booked wrong, and leaves tax depreciation to your preparer.

Watch someone use it

Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, fixed asset register and book depreciation, September 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

Claudewith the MosoFin fixed assets and depreciation skill

Can you update our fixed asset register for September and work out the depreciation?

Claude

Yes. Before I read anything, I need ten answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.

  1. Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
  2. Which period?
  3. Please attach your asset register, if you have one.
  4. What useful life, method and salvage value do you use for each class of asset?
  5. Do you book depreciation by your own policy, or post the figure from your accountant or tax return?
  6. What is your capitalization threshold? I never assume one.
  7. Which rule do you use for the first month: full month, half-month or pro-rata?
  8. Do you report under US GAAP, IFRS or local GAAP?
  9. Optional: which tax jurisdiction?
  10. Did anything happen that can reduce an asset's value? When did someone last count the assets, and who?

Use MosoFin. September. Register attached. Machinery 10 years, computers 3 years, no salvage. Vehicles 5 years, $5,000 salvage. All straight-line, by our own policy. Threshold $2,500, full month, US GAAP, US federal tax. No events. The operations manager counted in December 2023.

📄 fixed-asset-register.xlsx

  1. list_workspacesNorthbrook Trading
  2. get_agent_datasourcesNorthbrook Trading, no fixed-asset module

No business data read yet.

Claude

I found one workspace, Northbrook Trading, with one company file of the same name. No fixed-asset module is connected, so the register comes from your spreadsheet. Is that the right company file?

Yes, that's us.

Claude

Here is my plan. I run the register for Northbrook Trading for September under US GAAP. Your spreadsheet has six assets and the land at 31 August. Every class is straight-line, with a $2,500 threshold and the full-month rule.

The last physical count was December 2023, by the operations manager. I calculate book depreciation only. Tax goes to your tax preparer. Shall I start?

Yes, go ahead.

MosoFinChecked the tools, then read the booksread-only✓
  1. get_datasource_toolsRead tools only
  2. get_company_infoRead
  3. search_accountsLand has no accumulated depreciation
  4. get_balance_sheetRead
  5. get_general_ledgerAsset cost accounts, includes $17,550 on 8 Sep
  6. get_general_ledgerDepreciation, $1,550 posted on 30 Sep
  7. search_purchasesDelta Packaging Machines, 8 Sep
  8. get_profit_and_lossRead

8 calls. Nothing in your books changed.

Claude

Your register says $250,000 of cost at 31 August. The books say $244,000. I compare them both ways and keep two separate lists:

Tie-out, both ways
ListCostAsset
On the register, not in the books$6,000Server
In the books, not on the register$17,550Shrink-wrap machine, 8 Sep

An asset that is not on the register never gets depreciation. I remove the server only if you agree. Land has no accumulated depreciation, which is correct.

Claude

The machine went into service on 14 September. Its invoice from Delta Packaging Machines has three lines, but only one went to Machinery:

Shrink-wrap machine
Machine, posted to Machinery$17,550
+ Freight, posted to Freight-in expense$650
+ Installation, posted to Repairs and maintenance$1,000
= Full cost$19,200

Freight and installation make the machine ready for use, so Machinery is short by $1,650. With your full-month rule, September gets $19,200 ÷ 120 months = $160.00. Its book value at 30 September is $19,040.

Claude

Two items in Repairs and maintenance are at or above your $2,500 threshold. A large repair can be a real repair, so each one is your decision:

Threshold scan
Vendor and dateAmountDescription
Lift Services, 17 Sep$6,800Rebuild the forklift engine
CoolAir, 22 Sep$4,200Supply and install an office air conditioner

I also checked the other way. No asset account has an item below $2,500. Is each item a repair or an asset?

The forklift is a repair. The air conditioner is capital, machinery, in service 22 September. And yes, remove the server.

Claude

Thank you. One more problem. On 15 September you sold the old van for $4,000. The books removed its $30,000 cost, but not its $30,000 of depreciation:

Sale of the old van
Cash received$4,000
− Book value, cost less depreciation$0
= Gain on disposal$4,000

The books show a loss of $26,000 instead. That is a $30,000 error in profit. Vehicles also shows a negative book value of $12,400.

Claude

Your monthly entry posted $1,550 on 30 September, but it was out of date. Machinery showed an implied life of 12.1 years against your 10-year policy. I propose four draft entries:

Draft entries, not posted
EntryAmountEvidence
Add freight and installation to Machinery$1,650Delta invoice, 8 Sep
Depreciation on the shrink-wrap machine$160Your 10-year policy
Move the air conditioner from Repairs to Machinery, with $35 depreciation$4,200CoolAir bill and your decision
Remove the van's depreciation. Clear the $26,000 loss and record the $4,000 gain$30,000Sale of the van, 15 Sep

September book depreciation becomes $1,550 + $160 + $35 = $1,745, and the implied life is 10.0 years. You own seven assets with a book value of $161,705. A person posts these entries. I do not. Do you want the workpaper as an Excel file?

Yes, please.

Claude

Done. FA_Register_and_Depreciation_2026-09.xlsx has eleven sheets. They include both tie-out lists and the threshold scan. A clean tie-out does not prove that the assets exist. Your last count was December 2023, about 2 years and 9 months ago, so it is overdue.

Do you want me to save your settings for next month?

Yes, save them.

Claude

Done. I saved your class policies, the $2,500 threshold, the full-month rule, the account map, US GAAP and the count owner. I never save the register, costs or book values, or your connection and tool settings.
